Bridge and ramp junctions: real condition vs. the model

Vancouver Bikeway Designer v3 · review of 2026-09-29 · Granville, Cambie and Burrard bridges. Each section shows Google satellite imagery and Street View of the real junction beside the model before and after the fixes. Google imagery was used for looking only; the model is built from the City of Vancouver centrelines and OpenStreetMap lane counts and levels.

What was reviewed

Granville Bridge, north end (Drake St): Howe and Seymour ramps

Real condition: the six-lane deck (two-way bike path on the west side) reaches Drake St and fans into three roadways at one point — the Howe St on-ramp to the west, Granville St (four lanes) in the middle, the Seymour St off-ramp to the east. Street View from the deck northbound shows one continuous surface with the exit lanes peeling off behind a parapet; the ramps are two lanes each.

  • Data: City pieces 7316 (deck, OSM 6 lanes), 5860 (Granville St, OSM 4 lanes), 8289 Seymour ramp and 5407 Howe ramp (OSM 2 lanes each, right-of-way value 17.2 m). Fixed by taking the width from the lane count both ways.
  • Duplicate City centrelines (3154/5356, 5355/5405 on the approach; 5357/5406 on Howe St) drew two slabs on one line — one is dropped.
  • Granville St at Drake now lands at grade (the bridge piece falls over its last 73 m) instead of the at-grade block beyond Drake being lifted 6 m.
  • Remaining data limit: at Howe & Drake the City's Howe St pieces carry contradictory OSM end levels (the Howe St way is tagged as a bridge, the ramp way tagged at grade at the same node), so Howe St meets the ramp 48 m before Drake and falls at 12 %.

Granville Bridge, south end: Hemlock, Fir St and 4th Avenue ramps

Real condition: the deck lands on Granville St between W 4th and W 5th; the Hemlock St on-ramp (northbound) joins from the east; the southbound side leaves as one two-lane ramp that forks into the Fir St ramp (a long straight structure west of Fir St, descending to W 6th) and the 4th Avenue ramp (landing on W 4th Ave at grade). W 4th Ave passes under the deck.

  • Data: 9779 Hemlock ramp, 4615 Fir ramp (464 m), 6131 4th Ave ramp, 4885 southbound ramp: all had no OSM lane count and right-of-way widths of 15–23 m; now two lanes (7.2 m).
  • W 4th Ave (2766) was lifted to 6 m because the 4th Avenue ramp ended at its node; it now stays at grade and the ramp falls to it (landing rule).
  • The fork is an equal-width split (7.2 m into two 7.2 m ramps): each branch now merges into the trunk piece because it has a sibling at the node, so the gore between them is paved.
  • Remaining data limit: the at-grade Granville St service road under the approach (1900 Granville St) continues from a piece whose north end OSM tags as elevated, so it is drawn falling from the deck over one block.

Cambie Bridge, north end: Nelson St on-ramp and Smithe St off-ramp

Real condition: the divided deck (three lanes northbound, two southbound, median) passes over Pacific Blvd and splits — northbound traffic exits to Smithe St (east), southbound enters from Nelson St (west) — landing at Expo Blvd at grade. Street View from the deck northbound shows one wide surface with the Smithe lanes diverging behind a Jersey barrier and the southbound carriageway behind the median barrier.

  • Data: 6562 (two-way deck, OSM 5 lanes + median), 4616 northbound (3 lanes) and 6130 southbound (2 lanes) as one divided structure (twins); 10353 Smithe and 100 Nelson St at grade.
  • The landing rule brings each leg down to grade at its street; the fall starts past the streets each leg crosses over (Pacific Blvd), steepening to 12 % where the piece is short.
  • The mid-span split node is 480 m from the nearest designable block, beyond the 3D scene plate (±320 m), so it can only be seen from the block's own view edge.

Cambie Bridge, south end: W 2nd Avenue on-ramp and W 6th Avenue off-ramp

Real condition: the deck passes over W 2nd Ave; a northbound on-ramp from Cambie St / W 2nd climbs beside the deck's east side for about 170 m and merges at deck level; a southbound off-ramp leaves the west side and curves down to W 2nd Ave westbound (Olympic Village). Street View from the east sidewalk shows the deck with its railing and the parking lot below — the on-ramp is outside the sidewalk, not under it.

  • Data: 5858 / 6562 deck (5 lanes + median = 19.1 m), 8290 on-ramp (OSM 2 lanes, 7.2 m) 13 m from the deck centreline, 10391 off-ramp (3 lanes, 10.5 m).
  • The on-ramp now climbs 6 m over 170 m (3.5 %) — the climb must be complete before it passes over W 2nd Ave — and stays level beside the deck until its whole width is clear of the deck's carriageway before it is allowed to differ in height (the nose rule).
  • While its height differs from the deck's, its centreline is moved outward by the band overlap so the deck's sidewalk is never drawn above it; the shared height field now only evens out vertices within 0.5 m, so the ramp keeps its own grade (no twist).

Burrard Bridge: Pacific St (north) and Cornwall Ave (south)

Real condition: the five-lane deck (protected bike lanes both sides) lands at grade at Burrard & Pacific in the north and at Burrard & Cornwall in the south; the Pacific and Cornwall ramps are at grade around those intersections (not structures in the City's file).

  • Data: 2079 Burrard Bridge (1068 m, OSM 5 lanes = 17.1 m); 6841 1300 Burrard St and 1800 Cornwall Ave at grade.
  • No ramp merges into the Burrard deck in the City's file, so the junction fixes above do not apply; the landing rule and the two-ended profile are what changed here.

Design and upgrade of bike lanes on structures

As suggested, bridges, viaducts, overpasses and their ramps can no longer be selected for a new or upgraded bike lane: the block card explains why, and their existing facilities are still drawn and scored. A proposal now stops at the streets leading to a structure.
